observations: F1: mobile Safari, credit card, 2026-03-01, $120 → checkout failure
F2: mobile Safari, credit card, 2026-03-02, $85 → checkout failure
F3: mobile Chrome, credit card, 2026-03-03, $210 → checkout failure
F4: desktop Firefox, credit card, 2026-03-04, $45 → checkout failure
F5: mobile Safari, credit card, 2026-03-05, $310 → checkout failure
S1: mobile Safari, PayPal, 2026-03-02, $75 → checkout success
S2: desktop Chrome, credit card, 2026-03-03, $95 → checkout success
pattern: All failures use credit card; the sole credit card success is desktop Chrome; PayPal on identical hardware succeeds
generalization: Credit card checkout is failing across all tested browser/device environments except desktop Chrome; the bug is most likely in the credit card processor integration path for non-desktop-Chrome environments, not a blanket credit card outage
counterexamples: S2: desktop Chrome + credit card succeeded on 2026-03-03, ruling out a complete credit card processor outage

inductionSteps.intermediateGeneralization: All five failures share credit card as the payment method, spanning diverse browsers (Safari, Chrome, Firefox) and device types (mobile and desktop); credit card is the one antecedent present in every failure case

S1 uses the same browser and device as F1 and F2 (mobile Safari) but pays with PayPal instead of credit card and succeeds; with browser, device, and date held approximately constant, the payment method is the sole varying factor — strengthening the inference that credit card is causally implicated, not the platform

S2 (desktop Chrome + credit card) succeeds while F3 (mobile Chrome + credit card) and F4 (desktop Firefox + credit card) fail on the same or adjacent dates; credit card alone is not sufficient to cause failure — the failure requires credit card on a non-desktop-Chrome environment, indicating a browser/rendering-engine-specific bug in the credit card checkout path rather than a payment gateway issue
